assumptions: Utility function drift is quantifiable through task completion variance.
Feedback latency can be controlled via synthetic environmental delay.
Feedback latency impacts are distinguishable from random noise.
definition.falsification: Observed divergence variance remains statistically indistinguishable from baseline variance across all latency steps.
definition.statement: Increased feedback latency in intelligent systems, during the transition from plan formulation to solution execution, results in a non-linear increase in utility function drift, measured as task completion divergence from established success criteria.
definition.uncertainty: The baseline divergence under zero-latency conditions may be high, requiring calibration before establishing drift thresholds.

definition.method: Execute a synthetic task environment simulation with controlled feedback delay intervals [0, 50, 100, 200 ms] to measure divergence variance.
definition.stop: Measurement completion for all provided seeds and latency steps.
definition.success: Measurements successfully generated for all latency steps without runtime errors.
